articles.title: 保时捷推出 911 Carrera RS 2.7 联名咖啡机，售价 7911 美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，当地时间 11 月 5 日，保时捷宣布与意大利咖啡机制造商 La Marzocco 合作，推出了一款限量版 Linea Micra 意式浓缩咖啡机和 Pico 咖啡磨豆机，以及咖啡杯、咖啡师毛巾、服饰和汽车模型等周边产品。这款咖啡机以保时捷 1972 年推出的经典跑车 911 Carrera RS 2.7 为设计灵感，在机身顶部的杯架位置融入了标志性的鸭尾扰流板造型。这款咖啡机在美国市场税前价为 7,911 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 52,894 元人民币），欧洲为 5,790 欧元（现汇率约合 43,164 元人民币），咖啡磨豆机为 2,125 美元（现汇率约合 14,208 元人民币）或 1,550 欧元（现汇率约合 11,555 元人民币）。根据保时捷官方新闻稿，此次合作是双方继 2024 年首次联名之后推出的第二个系列。新款咖啡机采用 Porsche 911 Carrera RS 2.7 的经典配色和设计元素，压力表指针采用红色与绿色搭配，旋钮上印有 RS 和 2.7 标识，机身侧面还配有刻有“ONE OF 911”的限量版铭牌。Linea Micra 咖啡机提供三种经典保时捷配色：大奖赛白配绿色、大奖赛白配蓝色、橘色配黑色。其中大奖赛白配蓝色为德国市场独占，限量 150 台，另外两种颜色各限量 911 台。硬件方面，这款新品基于 La Marzocco Linea Micra 打造，配备可转换式手柄，可切换单份、双份和无底手柄配置。用户可以通过 La Marzocco Home 应用调节冲煮温度、设置相关参数以及预约冲煮时间。咖啡机配备 2L 水箱和 LED 照明系统，兼顾日常使用需求与外观设计。双方还推出了配套 Pico 咖啡磨豆机，提供与咖啡机相同的联名设计和配色。这款磨豆机支持三组研磨参数记忆、无级研磨粗细调节和手动研磨，并配备磁吸式可调节手柄支架以及自动闭合豆仓。除咖啡设备外，此次联名系列还包括咖啡香氛罐、咖啡杯、杯碟、咖啡师专用毛巾、服饰以及 911 Carrera RS 2.7 汽车模型等产品。其中，咖啡香氛罐售价为 135 美元（现汇率约合 902.6 元人民币），咖啡师专用毛巾售价为 69 美元（现汇率约合 461.3 元人民币），配套双人浓缩咖啡杯及碟套装售价为 105 美元（现汇率约合 702 元人民币）。保时捷确认，该系列新品已于 10 月 30 日起通过保时捷官网、部分保时捷中心及指定 Porsche Design 门店发售。

articles.title: 又一项重要成果，我国牵头制定脑机接口参考架构国际标准正式发布
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，据央视新闻报道，记者 6 日从国家标准委了解到，一项由我国牵头制定的脑机接口参考架构国际标准近日正式发布，这是我国在脑机接口国际标准化领域取得的又一项重要成果。报道称，该标准围绕“脑机接口是什么、怎么用、有什么功能、如何实现”四个核心问题，系统梳理了典型实现模式，形成包括概念、应用、功能和实现的完整技术框架。脑机接口参考架构国际标准起草人潘纲介绍，现在大家对脑机接口的定义，也在逐步地发展过程当中，早期脑机接口概念最主要就是意念的读出，现在经过二三十年的发展，它不单是读出，简单地说，其实是一个信号的读出来，去解读它，进而去调控、干预、影响它，这样形成信号的读出和写入的闭环。IT之家注意到，标准把脑机接口“怎么用”归纳为五类，包括实时感知人的注意力、疲劳、认知负荷等脑状态，可用于工业作业等安全预警场景。对于身体严重损伤或者没有办法交流的患者，通过脑机接口来跟外部机器人包括外控的轮椅实现打字、喝水这些日常的功能。脑机接口还可以与康复机器人等结合开展神经康复训练，促进脊髓损伤、卒中等患者运动功能恢复；通过神经反馈等方式帮助健康人开展注意力调节、认知训练等，提升或拓展原有能力；另外，将脑机接口与眼动、语音、手势、肌电等交互方式结合，还能形成更加准确、灵活的多模态人机交互。潘纲表示，现在脑机接口技术也到了从技术的突破逐步往产业转换的关键阶段。一个厂家是做不了所有的内容的，不同的部件，包括数据的格式都特别不一样，通过这个标准，让大家尽量能够在这个框架下去形成未来的整个产业体系。报道提到，我国已牵头发布三项脑机接口领域基础的国际标准，分别是术语、用例和参考架构。目前，我国正在牵头制定多项脑机接口国际标准。延伸阅读据 ISO 官网信息，此次发布的脑机接口参考架构国际标准编号为 ISO / IEC 27572:2026，全称为《信息技术脑机接口参考架构》，于 2026 年 9 月正式出版，共 18 页，由国际标准化组织（ISO）与国际电工委员会（IEC）下设的 ISO / IEC JTC 1/SC 43（脑机接口分委会）负责制定。ISO / IEC JTC 1/SC 43 于 2022 年 3 月成立，其前身是 JTC 1 第 16 咨询组（AG16），工作范围覆盖信息技术领域的脑机接口标准化，但明确将人体植入物及医疗应用标准排除在外。目前中国是该分委会 13 个参与成员（P 成员）之一。我国牵头发布的三项脑机接口领域基础国际标准中，术语标准为 ISO / IEC 8663:2025《信息技术脑机接口术语》，由中国医学科学院生物医学工程研究所专家蒲江波担任项目牵头人，我国于 2021 年 3 月提出提案、同年 9 月通过投票立项，先后有美、日、澳等 8 个国家参与，标准共梳理出基本概念、分类、信号、实验、应用等 8 大类 126 个词条；用例标准为 ISO / IEC TR 27599:2025，于 2025 年 5 月发布，共 108 页，收录了医疗健康、工业控制、智能环境等领域的代表性用例。文章中提到的标准起草人潘纲，是浙江大学教授，任职于浙江大学脑机智能全国重点实验室、计算机学院及良渚实验室，长期从事脑机接口、类脑计算等方向的研究。在国内层面，与之对应的国家标准为 GB/T 47023-2026《信息技术脑机接口参考架构》，由全国信息技术标准化技术委员会（SAC / TC 28）归口，起草单位包括浙江大学、中国电子技术标准化研究院、南湖脑机交叉研究院、天津大学、华为技术有限公司、电子科技大学、中兴通讯等，该标准于 2026 年 1 月 28 日发布、2026 年 8 月 1 日实施。

articles.title: 触控剪辑 / 调色登场：达芬奇 DaVinci Resolve 21.2 发布，适配苹果首款触控 MacBook Pro
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，Blackmagic Design 昨日（11 月 6 日）发布达芬奇 DaVinci Resolve 21.2 更新，同时更新 DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.2（付费版），为剪辑、调色和特效工作流带来触控支持等。达芬奇 DaVinci Resolve 是 Blackmagic Design 开发的专业视频后期软件，把剪辑、调色、视觉特效、动态图形、音频后期和照片处理整合在同一套应用中，常被用于短片、广告、纪录片、电影和自媒体内容制作。IT之家援引博文介绍，本次更新最值得关注的改进，在于原生支持苹果首款配备 PROLED XDR 屏幕的触控 MacBook Pro，创作者可以直接用手指滚动时间线、拖放素材、添加特效和字幕，并在检视器中缩放画面，让移动端剪辑与调色更接近“上手即用”的体验。性能方面，Blackmagic 称新版本在搭载 M5 Pro 和 M5 Max 芯片的设备上，可将特效渲染速度提升至最高 5 倍。对于经常处理高分辨率素材、复杂合成和大量调色节点的视频团队而言，这一优化有望明显缩短导出与预览等待时间。色彩工作流方面，DaVinci Resolve 21.2 新增支持 Blackmagic Generation 6 Color Science LUT 和胶片风格，ResolveFX False Color 则同时兼容 Gen 5 与 Gen 6 色彩科学，便于用户在不同摄影机素材和调色流程之间保持更一致的画面表现。编辑体验方面，多机位剪辑片段现可在源时间线中作为源片段打开；提取音频文件会保留源时间码；复合片段、PNG 的 EXIF 元数据等也得到改进。软件还针对音频、AAF、OGraf、H.265 和 XDCAM 媒体修复了大量问题，并包含超过 25 项稳定性与性能修正。Studio 版用户还将获得更完善的 AI 助手功能，包括在调色和 Fusion 操作中的扩展能力，以及脚本 API 改进。AI 助手可进一步处理帧和缩略图相关任务，帮助创作者减少重复操作。DaVinci Resolve 21.2 现已可通过 Blackmagic Design 支持中心免费下载；DaVinci Resolve Studio 仍采用一次性买断授权，售价为 239.99 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,605 元人民币）。

articles.title: 美国“空中外卖”竞争白热化：谷歌系 Wing 投资 1.25 亿美元建无人机厂，瞄准 270 家沃尔玛门店
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，谷歌母公司 Alphabet 旗下无人机配送公司 Wing 昨日（11 月 6 日）宣布，将在未来两年内投资最高 1.25 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 8.36 亿元人民币），用于在美国得克萨斯州沃斯堡建设并运营一座新一代无人机生产设施。该工厂面积约 1.5 万平方英尺，预计可创造至多 100 个制造业岗位，并具备年产数万架无人机的潜在能力。图源：WingWing 表示，这笔投资将主要用于直接制造，以支持其下一代配送无人机的本土化生产。新工厂将用于制造其下一代送货无人机，以支撑沃尔玛计划到 2027 年扩展至超过 270 家门店的无人机配送网络。Wing 目前已在达拉斯-沃斯堡都会区为沃尔玛提供配送服务，当地已有 19 家沃尔玛门店接入其无人机配送体系。这则消息发布的前一天，沃尔玛另一家无人机合作伙伴 Zipline 宣布完成 15 亿美元（现汇率约合 100.29 亿元人民币）融资，估值达 215 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,437.51 亿元人民币），并与沃尔玛签署新增 300 个配送站点的合作。Wing 现有“蜂鸟”（Hummingbird）系列配送无人机最高巡航速度为每小时 97 公里，最大载重约 2.3 公斤，可通过系绳将包裹降至指定地点。该公司称，其服务已覆盖全美 70 多个站点，今年已完成超过 100 万次美国家庭配送，并计划到 2027 年覆盖近 20 个都市圈、触达约 4,000 万美国用户。

articles.title: 马斯克 SpaceX 拟收购 Boost Mobile 切入传统电信运营商领域，AT&T 和 T-Mobile 据称已准备应对方案
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，Semafor 记者 Rohan Goswami 昨日透露，如果埃隆・马斯克旗下 SpaceX 成功收购 Boost Mobile，AT&T 和 T-Mobile 将可能切断这家运营商对其移动网络的访问权。由于 Boost Mobile 目前高度依赖 AT&T 和 T-Mobile 提供网络容量，这一潜在举措可能使 SpaceX 借助收购快速进入美国移动通信市场的计划面临阻碍。此前，《华盛顿邮报》11 月 2 日报道称，SpaceX 正与 Boost Mobile 母公司 EchoStar 商讨潜在合作，方案包括收购 Boost Mobile，或者直接获得其网络使用权限。据称，马斯克本人也参与了相关谈判，并于 10 月与 EchoStar 董事长兼首席执行官查理・埃尔根（Charlie Ergen）会面。根据 EchoStar 2026 年第二季度披露的数据，该公司拥有约 738 万移动用户，主要来自 Boost Mobile 和 Gen Mobile。通过收购 Boost Mobile，SpaceX 有望快速获得现有客户群及零售分销网络，而不必完全从零开始建立移动通信业务。不过，收购 Boost 并不意味着 SpaceX 可以自动继承其与 AT&T、T-Mobile 签订的移动虚拟网络运营商（MVNO）协议。LightShed Partners 分析师 Walt Piecyk 和 Joe Galone 发布的研究报告称，SpaceX 无法仅通过收购 Boost Mobile 就直接获得其与两家运营商的网络租赁协议。其中，Boost 与 T-Mobile 的 MVNO 合作协议将于 2027 年 7 月 1 日到期，因此 SpaceX 如果希望通过这笔交易获得长期网络资源，重点可能落在 AT&T 的网络协议上。但 AT&T 的合同同样存在限制。根据 EchoStar 与 AT&T 签订的网络服务协议，EchoStar 并不能自由地将网络转售给其他企业，相关条款还涉及受限制方（Restricted Party）的定义。如果 SpaceX 被认定属于受限制方，相关交易可能触发 AT&T 的合同终止权。据 Light Reading 11 月 3 日报道，即使 SpaceX 能够绕过控制权变更条款，继续使用 AT&T 网络，也未必能够保留 EchoStar 目前享有的优惠价。合同还规定，即使 AT&T 终止合作，EchoStar 仍可能拥有最长两年的过渡期，以继续为现有 MVNO 用户提供服务。MoffettNathanson 分析师 Craig Moffett 也对这项交易持谨慎态度。他认为，即使相关安排在法律上可行，AT&T 仍可能通过合同机制增加交易难度。AT&T 首席执行官 John Stankey 此前多次强调，Starlink Mobile 并不符合 AT&T 选择 MVNO 战略合作伙伴的要求。另一种可能的方案是，SpaceX 不直接取得 Boost 的控制权，而是先收购少数股权，以测试是否会触发合同中的控制权变更限制，例如 SpaceX 收购 Boost 49% 的股份，并将其更名为 Starlink Mobile。不过，这类交易结构是否能够避开合同限制，仍存在较大不确定性，也可能引发监管机构对市场竞争问题的关注。与此同时，SpaceX 并未放弃建设自己的地面移动通信网络。公司近期宣布将采用高通技术构建基站架构，显示其正在推进地面网络基础设施建设。不过，自建网络需要投入大量资金和时间，短期内仍难以完全替代现有运营商的网络资源。相关阅读：《消息称 SpaceX 洽谈收购 Boost Mobile，挑战美国电信三巨头》《马斯克 SpaceX 将收购全美低频段频谱牌照组合，美国三大电信股盘后跌超 5%》《高通史上最大 5G 交易：联合 SpaceX 建设星链移动全美国 5G 网络》

articles.title: 环比增约 70%：马斯克预估 SpaceX 第四季度营收逼近 250 亿美元，股价涨超 8%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，金融媒体 Barron's 今天（11 月 7 日）发布博文，报道称当地时间周五在纽约市林肯中心举行第 33 届巴伦投资大会上，全球首富埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）预估 SpaceX 第四季度（2026 年 10 月 1 日至 12 月 31 日）营收环比增长约 70%。IT之家此前报道，SpaceX 公司第三季度（2026 年 7 月 1 日至 9 月 30 日）营收为 145.75 亿美元，同比增长 161%、环比增长 86.52%。若以此计算，SpaceX 第四季度营收有望接近 250 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,671.53 亿元人民币）。马斯克同时重申，SpaceX 有望在 12 月实现 1,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 6,686.11 亿元人民币）的年化营收规模，并预计到 2027 年底年化营收将超过 5,000 亿美元（现汇率约合 3.34 万亿元人民币）。这一预测背后，SpaceX 的收入结构正在明显变化。马斯克称，本季度来自美国政府机构的收入占比将低于 10%，低于上一季度的 16.6%；人工智能算力业务则成为增长引擎，Anthropic 已是 SpaceX 单一最大客户。受上述表态影响，SpaceX 股价周五一度上涨 8.3%，盘后涨幅扩大至约 9%，创下近三个月最大单日涨幅。

articles.title: 工信部就机器人“身份证”暂行办法征求意见，全品类机器人“一机一码”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，工信部装备工业一司 11 月 6 日就《机器人产品标识码管理暂行办法（征求意见稿）》公开征求意见，公示期至 12 月 5 日。这份文件的核心是建立统一的机器人产品“身份证”体系，为每一台出厂的机器人赋予唯一的产品身份代码，支撑行业安全治理与全生命周期管理。根据征求意见稿，机器人产品标识码由制造商代码、产品说明代码、产品顺序号代码和其他代码四部分构成，编码与赋码须执行 GB/T 48541-2026《机器人产品标识码》国家标准。该国家标准的制定计划于 2026 年 1 月下达，由全国机器人标准化技术委员会归口，目前处于征求意见阶段。IT之家注：GB/T 为国家推荐性标准，企业可自愿采用，但一旦被行政规章引用，便在其适用范围内产生事实上的约束力。这一办法并非从零起步。2026 年 5 月，工信部人形机器人与具身智能标准化技术委员会已牵头发布全国首个人形机器人全生命周期管理服务平台，配套的《人形机器人全生命周期管理规范》采用 29 位四段式编码，依次为国家码、企业码、产品码与序列码，覆盖从出厂、流通、使用到报废回收的全链条追溯。截至 5 月，该平台已覆盖 100 余家企业、2.8 万余台人形机器人完成赋码。此次征求意见稿将标识码的适用范围从人形机器人扩展至全品类机器人，意味着工业机器人、服务机器人、特种机器人等均被纳入同一套编码框架之下。参考资料：《关于公开征求〈机器人产品标识码管理暂行办法（征求意见稿）〉意见的公示》

articles.title: 京东快递升级雪具寄递服务，最长免费暂存 7 天
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，京东快递 11 月 6 日宣布升级一站式雪具寄递服务，寄雪板立减 20 元起，全国近 30 个热门雪场最长免费暂存 7 天，提供上门取送、直达雪场和免费暂存等举措。为保障雪板、固定器等装备在运输过程中的安全，京东快递还提供专业雪具包装。价格上，寄雪板立减 20 元起，免除雪具超长超重附加费。服务上，支持快速上门取送与全国热门雪场直达。目前，京东快递已在张家口崇礼万龙、云顶、富龙，吉林北大湖、万科松花湖、武汉冰雪中心等多地雪场设立服务点、品牌形象店和移动揽收车。滑雪爱好者们进入京东快递 App 或小程序“雪具寄”入口，可一键筛选雪场填写收寄地址下单。针对部分用户提前寄送、抵达时间与雪具签收时间错位的情况，以及多雪场转场需求，京东快递还在全国近 30 个热门雪场提供雪具免费暂存服务，最长免费暂存 7 天。用户可根据行程灵活安排寄件时间，抵达雪场后再领取雪具，减少携带大件行李候车、转乘、排队托运以及多雪场转场的不便。滑雪结束后，也可预约快速上门取件，将雪具寄回家中。IT之家注意到，截至目前，新疆可可托海、阿勒泰将军山，河北张家口崇礼万龙、云顶、富龙等多地滑雪场已先后开板。

articles.title: Rust 重构安卓版 Discord 应用：2017 款 CPU 超低端手机也能“秒开 App”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，Discord 联合创始人兼首席技术官斯坦尼斯拉夫 · 维什涅夫斯基（Stanislav Vishnevskiy）今天（11 月 7 日）在 X 平台发布推文，分享了一段视频，对比演示了 Rust 重构开发的安卓版 Discord 应用。IT之家曾于 11 月 5 日报道，在内存涨价大背景下，Discord 弃用 Electron，改用 Rust 重写客户端，占用体积从 4GB 降至 290MB。在最新演示中，维什涅夫斯基在一台旧款手机（预估是三星 Galaxy A 系列）对比，现行客户端启动约需 3 秒、完整加载约需 5 秒；新客户端启动不足 1 秒，并在 2 秒内完成加载，流畅度明显提升。关于这款手机，网友 @Dolan245 补充表示演示手机是一款超低端手机，配备的是 2017 年的 CPU 核心。维什涅夫斯基随后转发该推文，认可了他的描述，表示：“展示一款启动时间仅需 200 毫秒的 iPhone，感觉就没那么有趣了;)”相关阅读：《内存涨价环境下 Discord 弃用 Electron：改用 Rust 重写客户端，占用体积从 4GB 降至 290MB》

articles.content: “IT早报”时间，大家好，现在是 2026 年 11 月 7 日星期六，今天的重要科技资讯有：1. 蔚来李斌再次警告车重，汽车重量增两成、路面损耗增至 2 倍李斌再度谈及整车重量问题。“有的车电池包堆 120 度，重量达七八百公斤，重对于车来说没什么，但大家算过对马路的影响吗？”李斌表示，“1.2 倍的重量，对马路的破坏就是 2.07 倍。”>> 查看详情2. 字节跳动出售沐瞳科技获市场监管总局批准，交易价格超 60 亿美元沙特电子游戏控股公司收购沐瞳控股有限公司等两家公司股权案获无条件批准，审结时间为 10 月 29 日。>> 查看详情3. 小米汽车架构调整：成立国际业务部，副总裁于立国兼任国际业务部总经理小米汽车近日宣布迎来架构调整，成立国际业务部，任命汽车部副总裁于立国兼任国际业务部总经理，向集团 CEO、汽车部总裁雷军和集团总裁卢伟冰双线汇报。>> 查看详情4. 地表最快量产车！比亚迪仰望 U9X 超跑极速挑战 503.17km/h 再创全球新纪录比亚迪仰望汽车官方微博 11 月 6 日宣布，仰望 U9X 阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战，以 503.17km/h 的成绩再创全球极速新纪录。官方预热海报宣称仰望 U9X 是“地表最快量产车”。>> 查看详情5. 2026 年中国金鸡百花电影节开幕短片《完美婚礼》首播，使用华为 Mate 90 系列拍摄华为终端 11 月 6 日放出了 2026 年中国金鸡百花电影节宣传片暨开幕短片《完美婚礼》及幕后特辑。据介绍，短片由黄建新监制、章笛沙执导，吴磊、庄达菲等全明星阵容参演，并使用华为 Mate 90 系列手机拍摄。这也是华为 Mate 系列手机已连续三年拍摄金鸡百花电影节宣传片。>> 查看详情6. 欧盟委员会称 TikTok 通过推荐算法制造信息茧房，要求整改“推荐”页面欧盟委员会初步调查认定，TikTok 的推荐算法让用户反复接触悲伤、孤独等负面内容，现有控制措施效果不佳。若拒不调整“为你推荐”页面设计，TikTok 最高可被罚全球年营业额的 6%。>> 查看详情7. 今日宜休鸿蒙版适配进度落后，王腾透露华为开发团队特意拉了小群来支持今日宜休科技公司创始人 11 月 6 日发文，称今日宜休鸿蒙版的适配进度落后。不过他透露，华为开发团队特意拉了小群来支持今日宜休。他表示，目前今日宜休在华为手机上卓易通版本已经上线，而纯血鸿蒙版正在开发中。>> 查看详情8. 全华班团队：比亚迪仰望 U9X“地表最快量产车”研发工程师揭秘，平均年龄不足 30 岁比亚迪仰望 U9X 阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战，以 503.17km/h 的成绩再创全球极速新纪录。IT之家从比亚迪官方获悉，本次项目的车辆研发工程师，均来自仰望内部研发团队，平均年龄不足 30 岁。这支“全华班”团队从 2024 年开始，伴随仰望 U9 及 U9 Xtreme 持续开展测试，逐步挑战世界纪录。>> 查看详情9. 微软 Win11 27H2 前瞻：改善 64 位应用性能、更换系统默认壁纸科技媒体 The Verge 11 月 6 日发布博文，报道称尽管外界持续期待 Windows 12，但微软目前似乎更倾向于继续深耕 Windows 11，正在筹备 27H2 重大版本更新，重点放在系统质量、性能和可靠性上。>> 查看详情10. 方程豹官宣钛 9 本月上市：比亚迪闪充技术 + 二代刀片电池加持钛 9 搭 DMS 混动平台，支持 5 分钟充好 9 分钟充饱，满油满电续航 1630KM，全系标配天神之眼 B，现车已备好，提车不用久等。>> 查看详情11. 苹果首款触控 MacBook Pro 教程：一条终端命令关闭发光 LOGO苹果公司 11 月 5 日更新支持文档，指出在配备 PROLED XDR 显示屏的苹果首款触控 MacBook Pro 上，用户可以通过终端（Terminal）命令，彻底关闭 A 面的苹果发光 LOGO。>> 查看详情12. 首款折叠 iPhone Duo 发售约 2 周后：苹果发起问卷调查，询问折痕、成像质量等核心体验科技媒体 MacRumors 11 月 6 日发布博文，报道称苹果首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo 发售约两周（10 月 23 日发售）后，公司已开始向部分购买者发送电子邮件调查，收集其对新机屏幕尺寸、折痕、屏下摄像头及其他功能的真实反馈。>> 查看详情13. 男子卖 3 台苹果 iPhone 18 Pro Max 赚差价，结果收到涉诈资金银行卡被冻结杭州冷先生首发日抢到 3 台 iPhone 18 Pro Max，转手闲鱼每台加价 750 元卖出。收

articles.title: 首飞失利 9 个半月后，谷神星二号遥三运载火箭发射成功
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，今日 7 时 37 分，谷神星二号遥三运载火箭在酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空，将搭载的观澜试验星、云遥一号 28 星、中北大学一号卫星、钧天一号 06A 卫星共 4 颗卫星顺利送入预定轨道，飞行试验任务取得圆满成功。IT之家注意到，这是谷神星二号在首飞失利后的复飞，距 2026 年 1 月 17 日遥一任务失败已过去约 9 个半月。谷神星二号由星河动力研制，是在谷神星一号基础上放大升级的中型固体运载火箭。火箭采用三级固体串联加液体上面级构型，高约 30 米，箭体最大直径 2.35 米，可选配直径 2.9 米和直径 3.35 米整流罩，起飞质量 100 吨，500 公里太阳同步轨道运载能力 1.3 吨。谷神星一号的对应运力为 0.3 吨，谷神星二号将这一数字放大了约 3.3 倍，使星河动力进入吨级运力发射服务市场，面向中小型星座组网与大型星座补网需求。相关阅读：《谷神星二号民营商业运载火箭首次飞行试验任务失利》《星河动力航天回应谷神星二号火箭首次飞行试验任务失利：全力查明故障原因》《星河动力航天：谷神星二号（遥一）运载火箭飞行故障通过归零评审》

articles.title: 苹果、英伟达等科技公司面临潜在国会调查，曾在特朗普白宫宴会捐款 2500 万美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，路透社昨日报道称，即将接任美国参议院常设调查小组委员会主席的民主党参议员理查德・布卢门撒尔（Richard Blumenthal），已经要求苹果、Meta、谷歌、英伟达、亚马逊和微软等参与特朗普白宫宴会捐款的科技企业主动提交相关文件，否则可能在 2027 年 1 月面临传票。结合华盛顿邮报当地时间 11 月 6 日报道，民主党议员正在为明年展开的一系列企业调查做准备，苹果、Meta 以及马斯克旗下企业均可能成为调查对象。部分企业高管已经开始寻求律师协助，以应对可能到来的国会传票和调查。苹果可能面临的调查之一，与其 App Store 下架 ICEBlock 等追踪 ICE 执法人员活动的应用有关。这类应用允许用户报告当地移民执法人员的活动，引发了有关执法人员安全和公众言论自由的争议。苹果此前已经因这类应用受到民主党议员质询。2025 年 10 月，苹果在美国司法部施压后，从 App Store 下架了 ICEBlock 及其他类似应用。苹果当时表示，采取这一行动是出于联邦执法人员安全方面的考虑。此前，美国得克萨斯州达拉斯一处国土安全部设施遭枪击，造成两名被拘留人员死亡，美国联邦部门将袭击描述为针对 ICE 的暴力事件。美国众议院司法委员会民主党首席成员杰米・拉斯金（Jamie Raskin）今年 9 月 29 日再次致信苹果，要求公司重新审查下架决定，并提供因联邦政府要求而从 App Store 移除的应用完整名单。拉斯金指出，苹果已经确认其下架 ICEBlock 的决定受到特朗普政府司法部施压影响，但司法部尚未提供能够直接证明该应用与达拉斯枪击事件有关的证据。他认为，此事可能涉及美国宪法第一修正案所保护的言论自由权利。另一项可能引发国会调查的问题，是苹果向特朗普白宫宴会厅建设项目提供的捐款。据《华盛顿邮报》披露，苹果和英伟达分别承诺向该项目捐赠 2,500 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1.67 亿元人民币），是已披露的主要企业捐赠方之一。路透社称，布卢门撒尔要求企业提供与宴会厅项目捐款有关的记录，以便调查捐款的具体情况及其与特朗普政府之间的关系。他表示，如果民主党明年 1 月正式掌握相关委员会的调查权，而企业仍未提交文件，委员会将考虑采取其他措施强制配合。相关阅读：《特朗普白宫宴会捐款名单曝光：苹果、英伟达各捐 2500 万美元为单笔最高金额》

articles.title: 消息称台积电考虑进军先进内存芯片制造，有望为英伟达打造 3D DRAM
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，科技媒体《The Information》昨日（11 月 6 日）援引两名知情人士报道，台积电正考虑扩大业务版图，进军先进内存芯片制造，以在快速扩张的 AI 硬件供应链中获取更大份额。报道称，台积电近期已应其最大客户英伟达的要求，开始规划生产一种名为“3D DRAM”的先进内存芯片。该架构通过垂直堆叠存储单元来提升容量，被视为应对 AI 算力对高带宽、高密度内存需求的关键方向之一。台积电目前尚未确定量产时间，也未最终决定产能来源。IT之家援引博文介绍，台积电正在评估两条路径：一是兴建专用新厂，二是收购现有晶圆厂并改造为内存生产设施。这一动向若落地，将意味着台积电从长期专注的晶圆代工、逻辑芯片制造，向三星电子、SK 海力士和美光长期主导的存储芯片市场延伸。对英伟达而言，若能获得更近的先进内存供应，也有助于缓解 AI 加速器所需高带宽内存的供应压力。不过，该消息仍属市场传闻。台积电回应称“不评论市场传闻或揣测”，并强调公司始终专注于晶圆代工核心业务；英伟达则未回应置评请求。

articles.title: 理想 Mega 新版本 MPV 谍照疑曝光，车头缩短、前三角窗加大
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，博主 @SugarDesign 昨日分享了一组新车谍照，猜测为理想 Mega 的新版本。从图上可以看到，该车车头变短，前三角窗更大。IT之家注意到，新一代理想 Mega Home 于 9 月 2 日发布，新车只提供一种配置，全国统一零售价 50.98 万元。作为参考，理想 Mega Home 可选灰 / 银 / 熊猫白 / 紫晶灰 / 新大象灰 5 种车色。该车新车前、后包围增加晶辉饰条装饰，新增智能三色星环灯提升精致感，车身长宽高分别为 5355*1965*1850mm，轴距 3300mm，提供 2.6m 长的 Sweet Home 超大迎宾光毯。内饰方面，新一代理想 Mega Home 搭载 29 英寸 OLED 6K 全景中控屏，二排带有 21 英寸 OLED 4K 移动屏。搭载高通骁龙 8797 智能座舱芯片，拥有 9.3.6 无瑕星环剧院音响系统。除此之外还带有 2 颗马赫 M100 芯片、4 个激光雷达，支持新一代马赫 VLA 司机大模型。此外，主副驾和第二排均配备零重力座椅。动力方面，新一代理想 Mega Home 采用前后双电机配置。前电机最大功率 155kW，后电机 258kW，综合功率可达 413kW 。配备 108kWh 三元锂 5C 超充电池，CLTC 综合续航里程可达 710km，10 分钟充电 500km。带有线控转向、后轮转向等功能，采用 800V 主动防倾魔毯底盘。

articles.title: 谷歌 YouTube 回应“半浅半深”界面：不是 Bug，测试“拼接”增强沉浸感
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，科技媒体 Android Authority 昨日（11 月 6 日）发布博文，经官方确认部分用户遇到的“一半深色、一半浅色”YouTube 界面并非 Bug，是一项正在小范围开展的界面实验。IT之家附上相关截图如下：根据社区用户反馈，安卓和 iOS 版 YouTube 在观看页面出现“一半深色、一半浅色”的奇怪界面，一度被误认为是应用故障。而最新官方回应表示，新设计将视频播放器和评论区改为“环境模式”（Ambient mode）。在这种模式下，界面会随视频画面的主色调动态变化，让播放器与内容更融合，营造更强的沉浸感。用户向下滚动后，推荐视频区域则会按照其系统或应用内选择的浅色或深色模式显示。该媒体解读指出，屏幕上半部分呈现随视频变化的色彩，而下半部分保持常规的深色或浅色界面，因此部分用户会看到明显的“拼接式”视觉效果。YouTube 表示，这项改动的目标是让观看视频的过程更具沉浸感，但目前仅面向一小部分用户开放测试，尚未公布正式推送时间。

articles.title: 苹果：超 10 万款应用已适配 iPhone Duo 折叠屏手机
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，据 CNET 今日报道，随着苹果 iPhone Duo 折叠机型面向普通消费者发售，不少新机用户发现：部分常用 App 并未针对内屏做好适配。对于一款采用全新硬件设计的手机来说，这类情况十分常见，众多安卓折叠屏设备也经历过相同阶段，App 完成适配往往需要一定周期，苹果证实现状正在改善。苹果全球开发者关系副总裁苏珊・普雷斯科特向 CNET 表示：“如今 App Store 上已经上线超过 10 万款适配 iPhone Duo 的应用，并且每天都有成千上万款经过优化的新应用上架。”“仅过去一个月，全球 19 座城市就有数千名开发者参与我们的线下技术工坊，亲手体验 iPhone Duo，为用户带来更新后的应用版本。”普雷斯科特说道，“开发者们热情高涨。随着越来越多应用完成对 iPhone Duo 的适配，应用更新的速度还会进一步加快。”在这些适配应用当中，微软 Word 与 Outlook 经过调整，界面效果接近桌面端版本；Zoom 则把内屏化作更大的视频会议画面。此外苹果确认，体育爱好者可以使用 NBA、NHL 官方 App，在大屏上观看比赛直播与赛事集锦。据IT之家此前报道，苹果在 2026 年秋季发布会上发布了旗下首款折叠屏手机 iPhone Duo，售价 15,999 元起。该机配备苹果迄今面积最大 iPhone 显示屏，展开状态亦是迄今最薄的 iPhone。iPhone Duo 还搭载 A20 Pro 处理器，拥有大尺寸 VC 均热板，号称相对 iPhone 17 Pro 持续性能提升 35%。

articles.title: 三星电子 DX 部门员工抗议奖金分配不公，要求现金补偿及管理层道歉
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，三星电子负责 Galaxy 手机、平板电脑、电视及家电业务的设备体验（DX）部门员工，因绩效奖金分配问题再次表达不满。据 Business Korea 当地时间 11 月 5 日报道，三星 DX 部门员工所属的“同行工会”（Donghaeng Union）近日在三星电子水原办公区外举行抗议活动，要求公司向 DX 部门员工提供现金补偿，并就此前的奖金分配争议作出道歉，同时要求建立面向 2027 年薪资谈判的联合协商机制。此次争议的核心在于，三星电子此前为负责半导体业务的设备解决方案（DS）部门员工设立了特别经营绩效奖金，而 DX 部门员工未能参与这项奖金计划。工会认为，现行薪酬安排导致两个部门员工之间的待遇差距进一步扩大。根据三星电子 10 月 29 日公布的 2026 年第三季度财报，DX 部门当季销售额为 52.1 万亿韩元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,598.23 亿元人民币），环比增长 8%，但营业亏损达到 8,000 亿韩元（现汇率约合 39.9 亿元人民币），连续第二个季度出现亏损。相比之下，受存储芯片价格上涨带动，三星半导体业务表现强劲。员工认为，存储芯片成本上涨增加了手机、电视和家电等终端产品的生产成本，尽管公司努力扩大产品销量，但仍未能抵消成本压力。根据韩国《联合通讯社》11 月 5 日报道，此次集会于当天 17 时在三星电子水原事业场中央门前举行。按照主办方估算，现场约有 1 万人参加。工会成员高喊要求公司解释销售额增长与巨额亏损并存的原因，并呼吁建立更加公平的薪酬制度。这场争议最早可追溯至今年 5 月的三星电子薪资谈判。“同行工会”当时退出联合谈判组织，理由是相关协商过于侧重半导体业务，未能充分反映 DX 部门员工的利益。随后，三星电子管理层与其他工会达成薪资协议，为 DS 部门设立特别经营绩效奖金，资金来源为该部门经营业绩的 10.5%。按照相关协议，DS 部门员工最高可获得每人 6 亿韩元（现汇率约合 299.2 万元人民币）的绩效奖金，而 DX 部门员工获得的是价值约 600 万韩元（现汇率约合 29,922 元人民币）的三星自有股票。两部门的奖励差距成为员工不满的重要原因。工会方面并不反对 DS 部门员工依据原有制度获得绩效奖金。工会宣传负责人金宝拉表示，相比单纯讨论补偿金额，目前更重要的是建立能够与公司管理层协商补偿方案的沟通渠道。她还担心，如果 2027 年薪资谈判继续由以 DS 部门为中心的工会单独进行，DX 员工可能连续两年无法充分参与协商。韩国《联合新闻》11 月 5 日报道称，三星电子员工正在推动成立第六个工会，涉及现有工会之间的内部矛盾以及半导体与消费电子部门的奖金分配争议。随着 2027 年薪资谈判临近，工会之间的谈判主导权和 DX 员工的利益诉求也成为新的争议焦点。

articles.title: Planet AI 邀你“向地球提问”：超 10 年卫星影像变化，一句话就能查
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，美国卫星数据公司 Planet 于 11 月 5 日推出 Planet AI 应用，结合大语言模型与超过十年的全球卫星影像档案，让用户使用自然语言搜索、观察和分析地球表面的变化。IT之家附上演示视频如下：产品目前可通过 ai.planet.com 免费使用，用户登录 Planet Insights 账号后，未来可使用更多高级功能。Planet 强调，所有 AI 结论均以可查看的原始卫星影像为依据，以降低“AI 幻觉”带来的误判风险。用户只需用日常语言描述问题，即可在全球范围内搜索目标地点、追踪其时间变化，并生成对比图或延时影像。与需要专业 GIS 技能的传统遥感工具不同，Planet AI 采用“地图 + 聊天”界面。用户只需提出诸如“找出某地区新增建设用地”或“追踪某片森林的变化”等问题，AI 会解析需求，在覆盖全球的矢量地图和月度影像拼图中定位相关区域，并呈现可核验的卫星影像结果。该应用提供三大核心能力：一是“搜索地球”，通过 AI 理解影像中的视觉特征，在大范围区域内定位目标；二是“探究变化”，回溯十年以上的历史影像，识别变化发生的时间，并提供并排对比或延时画面；三是“深度分析”，可自动调用 AI 智能体完成复杂分析，支持上传图像、CSV 等外部资料，并设置趋势追踪和定时报告。Planet 表示，早期测试者主要将产品用于生态保护、土地管理和环境合规。例如，保护团队可用它监测栖息地、发现非法侵占或火灾风险，并在派出巡护人员前核实毁林预警；合规团队则能按临近水道等条件，在数分钟内筛出需要优先检查的工业场所，而此类工作过去可能需要数天的人工 GIS 排查。Planet 将这一能力归入其“行星智能”（Planetary Intelligence）战略，即把每日卫星观测与 AI 相结合，近实时地理解地球变化。业内人士认为，这款产品标志着地球观测从“专业遥感分析”向“自然语言驱动的公共决策工具”演进。若影像覆盖、更新频率和结果可解释性持续提升，农业、灾害响应、城市治理、保险与基础设施管理等领域都可能成为其落地场景。

articles.title: Anthropic 研究称 Claude AI 智能体可以靠“做梦”变得更聪明
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，Anthropic 昨日（11 月 6 日）发布研究文章《The components of agent memory》，系统拆解 Claude 智能体如何跨会话记忆、筛选、纠错和整理知识。该研究指出 AI 智能体可借鉴人脑“睡眠整理记忆”的机制，在空闲时间反思历史记录、纠错并构建知识结构，从而显著提升长周期任务表现。该研究将智能体记忆分为会话日志、记忆笔记、知识表征（如 Wiki）和注入上下文四层，并引入“做梦”（dreaming）机制，让模型在两次交互之间的空闲时间回顾日志、修正错误、提炼规则和更新知识库。研究团队认为，AI 可像人脑在睡眠中巩固记忆一样，将即时经验逐步转化为可复用的长期知识。Claude 会在会话中标记重要事件或写入记忆笔记，但并非所有信息都值得保存，它需要判断哪些内容在未来真正有用。Anthropic 指出，记忆本质上是一种对未来的预测，例如记录一条已验证的规则，意味着模型预期未来会再次依赖它。在持续学习基准 CL-Bench 的数据库问答任务中，具备记忆能力的 Claude 模型表现明显优于无记忆基线。Claude Opus 5.5 和 Sonnet 5.5 在使用记忆后，平均得分分别达到 0.838 和 0.833，而二者无记忆基线分别为 0.655 和 0.644。更强的模型能够自主形成“失败 — 反思 — 验证 — 总结规则”的学习闭环。在《宝可梦红》游戏测试中，Anthropic 还发现“少而精”的记忆更有效。Claude Fable 5 仅维护 10 个记忆文件，却获得 4 枚徽章；而 Sonnet 3.7 写下 413 个文件，仅获得 1 枚徽章。研究认为，模型应优先保存策略、计划和经测试的规则，而非不断变化的屏幕状态。“做梦”机制还展现出纠错能力。当 Claude 错误记录了宝可梦中心的位置并因此迷路时，系统通过比对原始会话记录修正记忆，让其最终成功抵达下一座城市；未修正记忆的运行则反复折返，未能完成目标。在约 35 万份企业文档的测试中，Claude 通过多轮“做梦”逐步构建 Wiki。随着“做梦”规模从 2 次会话扩展到 128 次，25 个问题的达标率从 13% 提升至 48%；将 Wiki 与搜索工具结合后，综合得分从 54% 升至 61%。Anthropic 表示，智能体记忆仍面临何时写入、如何保持更新、如何避免错误累积等挑战。未来 AI 或将更善于在完成任务后“回顾经验”，把零散交互转化为可迁移、可验证的长期知识。IT之家附上参考地址The components of agent memory相关阅读：《告别知识截止日：谷歌让 AI 学会“睡觉”，边用边学还不忘旧知识》

articles.title: FIGS Beats Earnings as Demand Outstrips Supply, CEO Trina Spear Says

articles.title: Show HN: AJX – Find out where AI agents get stuck using your product
articles.content:
Hi HN. I made AJX (Agent Journey Experience). It is a CLI and skill bundle that you run to test what your product feels like to use from the point of view of an agent, and you get back a list of "asks" that would improve your product from an agentic usability perspective: so that agents spend less time, tokens and retries to accomplish tasks with it.How?
It works by having an outer loop (AJX harness skill + CLI) that controls an "inner loop": the agent that actually tries out your product. The outer loop investigates the inner loop once it finishes.To try it, copy the prompt from the main page into your favorite agent and it will install the skill and CLI and you can then trigger /ajx skill, give it a prompt and some simple configuration as text, and it helps you with the rest.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. We organize the library around this task: a reviewer compares the formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. Our experience is that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, and that simple automated tests on the statements can expose problems even in the established literature. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06984v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses. Abstract: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models (LLMs), orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06996v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The policy that converts runtime estimates of an autonomous agent's condition into operational authority is rarely specified or measured. We empirically characterize the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score (ARS), a weighted combination of runtime trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, onto discrete authorization levels through an asymmetric rule: escalation requires consecutive observations above a band edge plus a margin, while a sharp drop in readiness restricts authority at once. On one matched set of 100 Monte Carlo traces, we compare TRAP with static, trust-only, risk-only, and symmetric policies. articles.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. Darwinian evolution relies on natural selection, Lamarckian evolution adds inherited learning, and agent-directed evolution allows agents to generate and evaluate behavioral variants and choose how extensively to search. When learning is sufficiently effective, these mechanisms exhibit progressively faster adaptation. Abstract: Once an agent is live, teams want to know whether it is doing its job, not just whether it throws errors. Yet most evaluation is one-off: a benchmark run, a look at traces, a single score. Its conclusions neither check themselves nor reach the agent. We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents. It models evaluation as performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes, and it requires every level's conclusion to trace back to atomic data and to be computed by versioned rules. The method covers four levels of analysis (span, trace, conversation and engagement), measures along a spine of Execution, Substance, Trajectory and Results, treats Conduct as a constraint throughout, and uses Provenance and Adjudication components to certify the evidence and the evaluators. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07066v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. In this paper, we propose EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework that maximizes exploration objectives subject to a constraint that preserves established task performance. We solve the resulting problem using an epigraph reformulation that introduces adaptive exploration budgets. This approach separates intrinsic rewards from task objectives and regulates exploration through task feasibility. articles.content:

Abstract: A verified Dafny postcondition certifies that a formula holds, but it does not guarantee that the result was reached through genuine independent reasoning. We introduce a cross-agent formalization protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into a Dafny predicate, and an Implementer model writes an operational method checked against it. A same-model control establishes that even with no capability gap, independent re-extraction from identical text agrees only 59.3% of the time. Evaluating four model configurations on 96 clinical trial documents, we find that agreement is highly sensitive to how model capability is allocated across the two roles: the GPT-4.1-nano/GPT-4.1-mini configuration achieves 53.0% agreement when the stronger model is the Implementer, but only 14.3% when the roles are reversed. articles.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. We show how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can scale symbolic modeling and help overcome these engineering limitations. We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior---and apply it to model both human and machine behavior across hundreds of challenging reasoning problems. Analyzing these programs reveals that both people and machines tend to oversimplify, adopt rules that are partial explanations for their observations, and misinfer dependencies between problem features. These shared signatures are modulated by available resources, with reasoning effort predicting the extent to which machines simplify and explain their observations.

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. Abstract: When a tropical cyclone (TC) threatens several ports, preparedness planning depends on anticipating which ports are likely to be affected and where disruptions may last longest. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07372v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. articles.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07464v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked. The agent receives no data, so it must acquire data from the Web, build its own backtest under a data cutoff, and deliver verifiable results. Grading needs no reference answer. Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance via explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, yet this process introduces critical safety risks. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Uncertainty in resource reopening times complicates train holding and rerouting decisions when resource closures coincide with arrival delays and processing-time extensions. We develop a rolling-horizon distributionally robust model that updates predictions of the remaining closure duration as observations of disruption resolution become available. The model jointly optimizes train routes, sequences, and timings. It minimizes the worst-case expected total completion delay over an ambiguity set of scenario probabilities. Conditional cuts are constructed from resource-use patterns, and a graph neural network guides the order in which resource relaxation subproblems are solved. Abstract: Autoregressive decoding relies on the KV cache, whose memory footprint grows linearly with context length and caps batch size and throughput. Existing post-training methods exploit redundancy across tokens, layers, and feature dimensions, or lower numerical precision. Abstract: Optimistic Hedge, a multiplicative weight update with one step of extrapolation, is one of the most natural regret-minimizing dynamics for games, and characterizing its regret has been a longstanding open question. Abstract: Profit-maximizing Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand (AMoD) operators may exploit consumer surplus through excessive prices and underserve less profitable regions by relocating vehicles away from them. articles.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07125v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molten chloride corrosion has been studied for decades, yet reliable prediction across different alloys, salts, and test conditions remains difficult. In this work, 291 static molten chloride corrosion experiments reported in the literature were compiled into a structured dataset and used to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for corrosion-rate predictions. To better represent the differences in salt condition across studies, a Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) was introduced to bring the reported salt-treatment method, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition on a common numerical scale. A blended tree-based ensemble provided the most consistent predictive performance, achieving a cross-validated \(R^2\) of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm\(^{-2}\) day\(^{-1}\). The graded CSPI retained more useful information than a simple purified/unpurified classification and emerged as the dominant model descriptor.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07130v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved strong performance in many tasks by letting agents learn from nothing more than a reward signal. However, in more complex tasks, agents still struggle to learn good, generalizable policies, even with carefully designed rewards and abundant samples. We argue that this difficulty stems from the reward decoding burden: designers encode their knowledge of the desired behavior into rewards and penalties, and agents must infer this knowledge from long sequences of noisy scalars. To address this burden, we propose prescriptive policy learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents higher-level knowledge about the tasks, termed principles of behavior, such as how to maintain balance, how to accumulate energy, and how to land smoothly. articles.title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07155v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A proactive agent must decide what to ask before it acts. Exact lookahead values combinations of questions but is expensive and leans on a fitted model; a one-step score is cheap but can miss them. Our main finding: the need for depth often lies in how the hidden cause is described. A one-step score on the label can be blind to an interaction among answers. A score on a suitable latent cause is not, and where that latent encodes the decision it replaces most of depth at a fraction of the search. Described differently, the same problem can defeat the score while exact values do not move, so keep the latent small and check it against exact values. Probabilities learned from one language model's answers do not carry to another unless planning allows for both; those read from tokens are worth only a few labels.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conditional independence testing is difficult when dependence is weak, localized, or expressed through distributional changes rather than a global mean shift. Existing tests usually return a scalar statistic or p-value, which summarizes evidence against independence but does not describe where the conditional law changes. We propose QRCIT, a quantile-resolution conditional independence test that compares P(X|Z) and P(X|Y,Z) through a quantile deformation learned by a shared model. A lightweight residual quantile-flow model first learns the baseline conditional quantile law and then learns the additional deformation induced by Y, yielding a global predictive-gain statistic with conditional-randomization calibration and an inspectable deformation field over context and quantile level. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based proactive dialogue systems provide goal-directed support through sustained interaction. Fine-tuning their underlying models on externally supplied dialogue data introduces backdoor risks. Existing LLM backdoor studies primarily focus on eliciting an attacker-specified response upon trigger activation. We present an interactive backdoor attack framework that uses training-data poisoning to steer post-trigger, multi-turn interactions toward an attacker-specified objective. Poisoned fine-tuning dialogues implant a trigger-conditioned guidance-policy bias that ordinary user utterances can activate, without deployment-time prompt modification or further attacker intervention. Abstract: Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a form of latent communication between language models, combines a larger model's prompt representations with a smaller model's efficient generation, offering a promising way to balance capability and inference cost. articles.content:

Abstract: Policy-based decision benchmarks evaluate whether systems apply written rules to financial and operational cases. Yet a rule-following response can be marked wrong when the benchmark misstates the required decision. We audit nine public policy-based decision benchmarks through source tracing, program execution, and controlled checks. We find unsupported targets, reference errors that survive replay or propagate as solved steps, and evaluators that reject acceptable answers or credit incomplete decisions. To measure the scoring impact, we rescore unchanged model responses. On the 96 LegalBench SARA numeric cases, correcting the scorer raises acceptance by more than 80 percentage points for each of three models, without changing references or responses. Abstract: Genetic variants are routinely reclassified in ClinVar after a patient is tested, sometimes from uncertain to pathogenic, yet patient recontact is inconsistent, with no clear duty and responsibility diffused among labs, providers, and patients. Abstract: Automated feedback on classroom discourse improves instruction in professional and online teaching contexts, and recent work suggests that delivering similar feedback to learners may strengthen these effects by sharing responsibility for participation. Abstract: Approaches to authorship verification or attribution typically model the style of a document, asking whether two documents were likely written by the same author. Abstract: Cancer screening disparities persist across the U.S., yet the patient-reported barriers driving low uptake remain poorly characterized at scale. While clinical surveys capture structured responses, they miss the organic, unsolicited discourse where patients candidly describe real-world obstacles. In this paper, we conduct a large-scale analysis of over 56,000 posts across six cancer-specific Reddit communities to surface barriers to cancer screening among U.S. patients. We apply a pipeline combining keyword filtering, barrier triage, open coding, and codebook synthesis to systematically extract and categorize patient-reported barriers from 576 U.S.-located posts. Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated judges for evaluating chatbot responses. We train soft prompts on the FairBotBench benchmark and evaluate the adapted judges across the dimensions of bias, toxicity, and personalization. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper proposes a trustworthy computational method to gender-swap public domain novels, with programmatic guarantees that only gendered words are inverted and all other words are left unchanged. This may seem like a simple task, but both large language models and naive rule-based methods fail to complete it. The proposed method includes a custom whitespace-preserving tokenizer, gender-swap mappings across plural and possessive forms, pronoun handling, and a character renaming strategy. It shortens the time required to gender-swap a novel from weeks of manual labor to minutes. The method is demonstrated on two public-domain novels. Pride and Prejudice is transported to matriarchal Regency England, where inheritance flows through daughters, mothers rule the household, and a frantic Mr. Bennet is determined to secure advantageous marriages for his sons. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07203v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier evaluations of tool-using conversational agents are conducted almost exclusively in English, leaving a critical gap for organizations deploying agents in other languages and regions. We present ${\tau}$-bench-LILT, a multilingual extension of ${\tau^3}$-bench covering German, Korean, Turkish, and Farsi in the airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains. We natively localize every layer of the benchmark: customer databases are populated with culturally appropriate records, user-simulator prompts are refined iteratively through contrastive annotation by native-language experts, and tasks are updated according to the localized database and to reflect realistic tasks in the target region. Evaluation across eight agent models shows the largest drops compared to English in the Korean and Farsi retail domains, by up to 61 points in pass^4. Abstract: Adolescents are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, advice, and companionship, raising safety concerns. Abstract: User inference asks whether a source contributed documents to a language-model update, even when the auditor observes only fresh documents from that source. Abstract: At context lengths of about 1M tokens, dense attention is costly in prefill and decoding, and training typically relies on long documents, which become scarcer as the target length increases. Most sparse attention methods score all preceding blocks or tokens, so their selection cost per query is $O(L)$ at context length $L$; hierarchical selection reduces it to $O(\log L)$, but prior trainable hierarchical methods report accuracy only within their training length. Abstract: We validate our previous hypothesis that a language model holds relational patterns apart from the subject domains that instantiate them (Nordfors, 2026). These archetypal contexts are patterns of relations that people recognize across many fields, such as the tipping point or winner takes all, held once and applied across domains. Abstract: AI agents may consume massive tokens across a wide range of tasks, but how many of those tokens are really necessary? Abstract: Parallel block drafting accelerates speculative decoding by predicting multiple future positions in a single backbone pass, but on-device deployment constrains both drafter capacity and context storage. Abstract: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language model responses by spending additional computation at inference time, and the right amount of compute depends on the prompt. articles.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. articles.title: T$^2$-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Triangle-based splatting connects novel view synthesis with conventional graphics pipelines, but often requires excessive tessellation to preserve appearance details. We present T$^2$-Splat, which decouples topology adaptation from appearance refinement. Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation (Safe RDT) initializes mesh connectivity. Dynamic Topology Evolution (DTE) then adapts triangle allocation through edge collapse and vertex split operations. Residual per-face Mip-textures then refine appearance on the fixed mesh using scale-adaptive filtering. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and DTU demonstrate competitive results with compact meshes. T$^2$-Splat improves PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360. Additional compression experiments demonstrate flexible control of mesh complexity, supporting face budgets as low as 10% of the original face count. Project page: https://t2-splat.github.io/.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06993v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Transductive adaptation improves vision-language models at test time by refining predictions on an unlabeled batch, but current methods face a key trade-off. Aggressive approaches exploit batch structure but can drift when batches are sparse, have prior shift, or cover little of the label space. Conservative methods better preserve CLIP text semantics, but fixed semantic references can under-adapt even when the batch provides strong corrective evidence. We propose JPTA (Joint Prior and Transport Adaptation), a prior-aware framework that casts transductive VLM adaptation as batch-conditioned semantic reference estimation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video understanding models often rely on motion, yet their explanations can obscure which motion sources support a prediction. We identify motion-source under-specification as a limitation of existing video XAI: region-centric explanations can be source-ambiguous, while motion vocabularies restricted to single-person pose sequences are source-incomplete. We propose TraCE (Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding), a concept-based framework that discovers source-flexible motion concepts by clustering optical-flow trajectories from training videos. These concepts represent dynamic evidence from people, objects, and interactions, while object and scene concepts account for static context. The resulting typed trajectory/object/scene interface supports class prediction for action recognition and question-conditioned concept matching for video question answering (VQA). Abstract: Hybrid Mesh-Gaussian rendering combines compact textured surfaces with flexible 3D Gaussian primitives, offering an efficient alternative to purely Gaussian scene representations for structured environments. Existing scene-reconstruction hybrids commonly follow an additive formulation, where Gaussian residuals compensate for errors left by the mesh. However, not every Mesh-Gaussian conflict is caused by missing content: residual geometry errors, occlusion mismatch, texture-projection artifacts, and view-dependent appearance can make the same mesh content consistent in one view but inconsistent in another. Abstract: Flow matching (FM) generators often face a quality-coverage tradeoff. Inference-time techniques such as classifier-free guidance raise quality, but at the cost of coverage. We hypothesize this limitation stems from a basic property of the objective: an intermediate noisy image could correspond to many clean images, yet the model can only predict a single velocity, at best averaging over the multiple possibilities. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07063v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models must balance two competing goals: learning fine-grained visual distinctions from very limited supervision and preserving the efficiency that makes frozen CLIP-like models attractive for deployment. Existing lightweight adaptation methods, including prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters, typically supervise global image embeddings and therefore underuse token-level structure. Conversely, structure-aware methods exploit local evidence but often introduce additional inference-time computation. We propose SD-LoRA, a structural distillation framework that uses token-level graph reasoning only during training and transfers its effects into a lightweight LoRA-adapted CLIP model. arXiv:2611.07081v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-perspective-camera systems are widely adopted since they provide broad visual coverage for autonomous driving, motivating the synthesis of a unified wide view from spatially separated observations. In this work, we formulate wide view synthesis (WVS), which aims to synthesize a geometrically consistent wide view at a specified virtual viewpoint from multiple perspective cameras. Unlike conventional image stitching, WVS requires reasoning about 3D geometry and visibility to handle depth-dependent parallax and occlusions arising from spatially separated camera centers. While vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-fidelity view synthesis, its reliance on per-scene optimization limits its applicability to driving scenes. Abstract: We present an automated method for auditing text-to-image generators for representational bias against ground-truth demographic benchmarks. We classify each generated image by race and then compare the model's distribution to publicly available demographic benchmark data to identify patterns of over- and under-representation. articles.content:

Abstract: Self-supervised learning has given rise to vision foundation models that learn general-purpose image representations transferable across downstream tasks, yet representation learning for 3D scenes has not achieved comparable success. Motivated by this, we identify key limitations of current 3D representation learning approaches and revisit their core design choices. We first replace the commonly used hierarchical PTv3 backbone with the Volume Transformer, a ViT-like architecture for 3D scenes. We then redesign two core objectives of modern approaches built around student-teacher networks: matching representations across views and predicting masked content from visible context. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07188v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Radiologists read a screening mammogram by first forming a global impression of the four views and then selectively magnifying suspicious regions before assigning a BI-RADS assessment. MLLMs, in contrast, see the whole image at a fixed, reduced resolution, which makes sub-millimeter calcifications invisible, and they perform close to chance on mammography. Therefore, we present MammoSeek, a mammography agent that reproduces this reading process. After forming an impression of each breast, the agent performs selective zooming: it decides by itself which detector candidates deserve a closer look and inspects only those on full-resolution views. Guided by a BI-RADS assessment skill, it then assigns a category and generates a localized, lexicon-structured report for each breast; its assessment is combined with image-model scores in a decision layer to decide recall. articles.content:

Abstract: Reinforcement learning has become an effective approach for improving video generation, but its success depends heavily on reliable reward models. Abstract: Single image dehazing requires recovering scene radiance from visual responses that are weakened and veiled by participating media. articles.title: ELA: End-to-End Latent Action Policy Learning from Video Demonstrations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05571v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding. ELA jointly trains a latent action model, latent action policy, and action decoder, enabling policies to leverage abundant video data with only a handful of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Abstract: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High motion performance and avoiding structural vibrations rely on smooth trajectory planning. The smoothness requirement depends on the robot's complexity in terms of the number of degrees of freedom and system order due to the flexibility of the joints and links. For industrial robots, the smoothness requirements have been determined and subsequently taken into account. Although unknown for soft continuum robots, the exact smoothness requirement can potentially be much larger than previously considered ones such as $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^4}$ for collaborative robots and $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^5}$ for quadcopter drones. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05667v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. During takeover, PHIL continues querying the policy and displaying its predicted trajectories in the physical workspace through an extended reality (XR) interface. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. Abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. Abstract: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. OUCH combines stacked pneumatic pouch actuators, a rigid indenter, and a compliant spacer designed to buckle at a set load, so that the indenter contacts the skin only during actuation. Abstract: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05793v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. Abstract: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) support planning by comparing predicted latent states with an encoded goal. articles.title: Does RRT* Work on Uneven Terrain Meshes?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05885v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The optimal rapidly exploring random tree (RRT*) is proven asymptotically optimal on open subsets of Euclidean space with straight-line local planning. We ask whether it works on a triangle-mesh terrain, a two-dimensional surface in R^3. First, the original RRT* cannot run on a mesh: the surface has zero volume, so uniform sampling never hits it, no clearance ball fits in it, and chords across a fold leave it. Abstract: An ordered sequence of end-effector poses can give a redundant robot arm multiple valid joint configurations at each waypoint. Inverse kinematics (IK) computes these configurations. Choosing a configuration only for the next waypoint can leave the arm poorly placed for later waypoints. This may increase planned motion time or cause a later planning failure. This paper presents Future-Window Inverse Kinematics (FWIK), an online method that selects IK solutions by considering a small window of future waypoints. A learned model removes paths whose transitions are likely to cause self-collision. Abstract: Off-policy deep reinforcement learning trains on random samples from a replay buffer of past experience. articles.content:

Abstract: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. Five photoemitters and five RGBW photoreceivers are mounted on opposing circuit boards coupled through translucent silicone. Load-induced interlayer motion modulates the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. A compact multilayer perceptron reconstructs three force and three moment components from 20 optical channels. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual-inertial odometry relies on visual features that correspond to 3D points with consistent projections across sequential frames. In reflective indoor-floor environments, however, specular floor patterns can be detected and triangulated as virtual features below the physical ground plane, producing unreliable feature associations and inconsistent visual residuals. This paper proposes a lightweight reflection-aware front-end for feature-based stereo VIO. Rather than suppressing all floor-region features, the proposed method estimates the ground height in real time and rejects only feature candidates whose inferred 3D positions are below the estimated ground height. articles.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

articles.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
articles.content: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines, including on transformer-encoded embeddings. We then apply the method to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.

articles.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
articles.content: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. A single multimodal judge evaluates six dimensions of communication and design, with three repeated judgments per figure. We attempt source-constrained revisions of all 371 figures, of which 369 pass the recorded fidelity checks. Original-figure ratings show no uniform decline across periods. Revisions increase mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and decrease aesthetic coherence ratings by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. Gains in the six-dimension average are larger for main-sample motivation figures than for frameworks. Case analyses show that added explanation can clarify comparisons while leaving typographic hierarchy and visual economy unresolved. These model-based findings support researcher-led design, with AI assisting exploration and authors retaining responsibility for explanatory purpose, composition, and scientific relationships. The accompanying atlas and evaluation records are available at https://ntu-ai4x.github.io/Rethinking_Figures/index_en.html.

articles.title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
articles.content: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. To do so, we introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a model uses its outputted grounding in its thinking trace and perform a detailed ablation study of a grounded reasoning training recipe. We find that grounded reasoning improves counting but shows no significant gain over baselines without coordinate grounding across a wide range of spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks. Using several synthetic tasks, we show that grounded reasoning is most useful when a task requires undescribable references, which are visual concepts that are difficult to describe in language. However, we observe that many existing visual reasoning benchmarks are solvable with only describable text references. To close this gap, we introduce BrickVision, a new benchmark that requires undescribable visual references to solve.

articles.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
articles.content: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.

articles.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
articles.content: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.

articles.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
articles.content: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video learning, making metric motion usable as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target. Cross-stream action-video coupling establishes close correspondence between metric motion and visual dynamics through lightweight adaptation while preserving the pretrained visual prior. Together, these designs establish a generalist framework spanning five action-video tasks. Despite adaptation only on controlled laboratory recordings, EgoGeneralist generalizes to diverse unseen scenes and interactions with effective action control and visual quality, bridging pretrained visual knowledge and metric 3D human motion.

articles.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
articles.content: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and challenging. We introduce XStack, a benchmark that evaluates agents on migrating ML repositories between these two ecosystems. Each agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a JAX repository. Its output passes if it meets our grading criteria, based on the source repository's published result, authenticated and calibrated by us. Migration by agents remains unreliable: Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and every other agent at most 40%. XStack is a step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem. We release XStack to make progress toward reliable migration across frameworks and hardware measurable.

articles.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
articles.content: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.

articles.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
articles.content: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. Our objective is to maximise the cosine similarity of a supplied residual stream direction with the activations of the text generated by the MAEM. This label-free RL objective helps to scale MAEMs on diverse sources of residual stream directions. Empirically, we find the resultant metamodel produces informative exemplars: a Qwen3.6-27B MAEM inverts held-out activations better than corpus search or a natural-language autoencoder (NLA), beats corpus search (at 10M tokens) on a majority of held-out languages/domains, and activates 89% of held-out SAE features. It also identifies concepts behind steering vectors about as well as NLAs, recovers the payloads of LoRA backdoors more often than corpus search, and can even verbalise some model workspace inner monologue. Unlike explanations produced by other metamodels (e.g. NLAs), MAEM exemplars can be verified with a forward pass on the subject model, making the MAEM objective a grounded alternative for scaling the training of metamodels.

articles.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.

articles.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.

articles.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
articles.content: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT dynamics of GD with large constant step sizes. We first study GD in adversarial linear logistic regression, focusing on two aspects: where the model parameters converge (implicit bias) and how quickly the losses decrease (optimization). We then turn to neural networks training and study how the sharpness of losses evolve during AT. Our results advance the understanding of the behaviors of GD with large step sizes in AT and highlight three key differences from its behavior in Standard Training (ST): (i) the implicit bias gap between AT and ST, previously established only for small step sizes, persists for arbitrarily large constant step sizes, (ii) different from ST, there is no uniform rate of convergence for the optimization error in AT, and (iii) sharpness can exhibit two-stage dynamics that differ from the Edge-of-Stability behavior observed in ST.

articles.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
articles.content: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain. Multi-teacher OPD (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student that matches each expert's accuracy, with the distillation stage costing only 5.2% (on 2 domains) and 8.0% (on 4 domains) of the specialist training FLOPs. Counting specialist training and distillation together, this pipeline reaches joint GRPO's performance on the 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.

articles.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
articles.content: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, anchored by five human-verified reference scores per task. Agents attempt tasks in fresh sessions with raw code or refined artifacts; a separate Auditor checks execution evidence. Across four evaluated models, refined artifacts raise mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduce downstream API spending by 19.7% on average. The cross-model success-rate spread narrows from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points, with all four models achieving mean success rates above 90%. Removing any component reduces success in the ablation study, with the largest losses from code and environment removal. These results suggest that preserving execution knowledge helps even models with lower raw-code success reproduce experiments more reliably and at lower API cost.
